All 52 units had zero movement left (already acted this turn), so my levers were production, research, policies, and the Congress. Here's what I found and did.

**The key play — science policy cards.** I'm pursuing a science victory and had *zero* science cards slotted. All three economic slots held gold cards (Market Economy, Free Market, Economic Union) while already sitting on +985 gold/turn with nothing to spend it on. I swapped them to Rationalism, Five-Year Plan, and Trade Confederation. Verified: **science 489.7 → 553.1 (+13%)**, costing gold I don't need (985 → 887). Five-Year Plan also boosts Daegu's Industrial Zone, so it pays twice.

Worth flagging: `set_policies` silently rejected all three swaps when batched in one call, reporting the old cards back. Applying them one at a time worked. That's a real tool bug — the batch path fails quietly, and the warning it emitted was the only reason I caught it.

**Two things I checked and correctly did *not* do:**
- Daegu (pop 20, my #2 production city) produces only 16 science with no Seowon, and Gwangju only 11. Looked like a glaring gap — but the district advisor returned no valid placement tiles for either. Both cities are too built out. The gap is structural, not fixable, so I left their production alone rather than churn it.
- The World Congress reports "IN SESSION (vote required!)" but returns no resolutions. Notifications clarify it's in the *proposal* phase and actually convenes inside `end_turn` — there's genuinely nothing votable yet, despite the alarming message. My 1765 favor stays banked.

**Left as-is deliberately:** research on Nanotechnology (3 turns → unlocks the Mars Colony project, correct for the space chain); Daegu finishing Chichen Itza this turn; three spaceports already under construction in Gyeongju (11t), Jeonju and Chuncheon (16t) — parallel spaceports let space projects run concurrently, which is the right build.

**One unresolved item:** 3035 gold is idle with no good sink. Districts can't be gold-purchased, and every science city already has its University and Research Lab, so I found no purchase worth making rather than spend it badly. The real bottleneck is spaceport *production time*, which gold can't touch. Pingala in Gyeongju has the "Space Initiative" promotion available (+30% production to space projects — directly on the critical path), but I have 0 governor points; that's the first thing to spend a point on when one comes up.

One-line summary: Turn 303 as runaway leader (score 1368 vs 852) — fixed a major misallocation by swapping three redundant gold policy cards for science ones (+13% science, verified), confirmed the Congress has nothing votable yet and Daegu/Gwangju physically can't take Seowons, and left the three-spaceport science plan running.

## What I found and did

**The World Congress blocker is not resolvable from my side.** `get_world_congress()` reports `IN SESSION (vote required!)` and my 1765 favor, but enumerates **zero resolutions** — no hashes, no options, no targets — across five separate calls, including after `dismiss_popup` (which found nothing to dismiss). `queue_wc_votes()` requires a resolution hash, and I won't invent one: a wrong hash either silently fails or misdirects favor. Notifications show the session sitting at "New Discussion Available for Proposal," which suggests the game is still in the proposal/discussion stage where resolutions aren't yet queryable. **This needs a tooling fix or an interactive vote — the 1765 favor is stranded.**

Since the blocker was immovable, I checked what else was actionable. All 52 units had 0 moves (unit phase already spent), and research was already correct: Nanotechnology unlocks the Mars Colony project, and Cold War leads to the Space Race civic. Three Spaceports are in progress.

The one real gain: I swapped **Levée en Masse → Natural Philosophy** in a wildcard slot. Levée en Masse only cuts unit maintenance, which is worthless when I'm at peace with every civ and hold 2965 military against a best rival of 660. Natural Philosophy stacks with Five-Year Plan on my five Seowons. Verified: **science 553 → 571 (+18/turn)** for −76 gold/turn — a good trade when I hold 3035 gold at +811/turn with no sink and science is the victory path.

Two tooling bugs worth logging beyond the Congress one: `get_cities` lists `CAN ATTACK` targets that are actually 3 tiles away (city range is 2 — both attacks I attempted were rejected as `OUT_OF_RANGE`), and `get_city_production` offers Gwangju a `DISTRICT_SEOWON` that `get_district_advisor` says has no valid placement tile.

**One-line summary:** Could not clear the World Congress blocker — the tool reports the session in progress but returns no resolutions to vote on, stranding 1765 favor; verified the science-victory path (research, civic, 3 Spaceports) was already optimal and swapped a dead military policy for Natural Philosophy, gaining +18 science/turn.

All 52 units had zero movement left (already acted this turn), so my levers were production, research, policies, and the Congress. Here's what I found and did.

**The key play — science policy cards.** I'm pursuing a science victory and had *zero* science cards slotted. All three economic slots held gold cards (Market Economy, Free Market, Economic Union) while already sitting on +985 gold/turn with nothing to spend it on. I swapped them to Rationalism, Five-Year Plan, and Trade Confederation. Verified: **science 489.7 → 553.1 (+13%)**, costing gold I don't need (985 → 887). Five-Year Plan also boosts Daegu's Industrial Zone, so it pays twice.

Worth flagging: `set_policies` silently rejected all three swaps when batched in one call, reporting the old cards back. Applying them one at a time worked. That's a real tool bug — the batch path fails quietly, and the warning it emitted was the only reason I caught it.

**Two things I checked and correctly did *not* do:**
- Daegu (pop 20, my #2 production city) produces only 16 science with no Seowon, and Gwangju only 11. Looked like a glaring gap — but the district advisor returned no valid placement tiles for either. Both cities are too built out. The gap is structural, not fixable, so I left their production alone rather than churn it.
- The World Congress reports "IN SESSION (vote required!)" but returns no resolutions. Notifications clarify it's in the *proposal* phase and actually convenes inside `end_turn` — there's genuinely nothing votable yet, despite the alarming message. My 1765 favor stays banked.

**Left as-is deliberately:** research on Nanotechnology (3 turns → unlocks the Mars Colony project, correct for the space chain); Daegu finishing Chichen Itza this turn; three spaceports already under construction in Gyeongju (11t), Jeonju and Chuncheon (16t) — parallel spaceports let space projects run concurrently, which is the right build.

**One unresolved item:** 3035 gold is idle with no good sink. Districts can't be gold-purchased, and every science city already has its University and Research Lab, so I found no purchase worth making rather than spend it badly. The real bottleneck is spaceport *production time*, which gold can't touch. Pingala in Gyeongju has the "Space Initiative" promotion available (+30% production to space projects — directly on the critical path), but I have 0 governor points; that's the first thing to spend a point on when one comes up.

One-line summary: Turn 303 as runaway leader (score 1368 vs 852) — fixed a major misallocation by swapping three redundant gold policy cards for science ones (+13% science, verified), confirmed the Congress has nothing votable yet and Daegu/Gwangju physically can't take Seowons, and left the three-spaceport science plan running.
